1282a.task_statement: Answer user inquiries regarding computer software or hardware operation to resolve problems.
1282a.part_text: Answer a user's question about software or hardware operation while the user is on the phone, in chat, or at the desk, resolving the problem during the contact.
1282a.work_item: one user call, chat, or walk-up question answered
1282a.start: user calls, opens a chat, or walks up with a question
1282a.end: user confirms the answer or fix works, or the issue is logged for follow-up
1282a.checked_by: the user who asked; help-desk supervisor through call reviews
1282a.split_reasoning: One activity, answering a user's question about software or hardware, but it is done in two places: live while the user is on the phone or at the desk, and afterwards from emailed or ticketed questions.
1282a.type_reasoning: The user waits while the specialist explains or walks them through the fix, so this is work done in a live contact.
1282a.unit_reasoning: Each call or walk-up is one contact that ends with the user's question answered or the problem handed on.
1282a.notes: Live versus written share depends heavily on whether the desk is phone-first or ticket-first; 1288 covers the investigation behind harder questions and overlaps substantially.

1282b.task_statement: Answer user inquiries regarding computer software or hardware operation to resolve problems.
1282b.part_text: Answer a user's emailed or ticketed question about software or hardware operation.
1282b.work_item: one written user question answered (ticket or email)
1282b.start: question received by email or in the ticket queue
1282b.checked_by: the user who asked; help-desk lead reviewing ticket quality
1282b.split_reasoning: One activity, answering a user's question about software or hardware, but it is done in two places: live while the user is on the phone or at the desk, and afterwards from emailed or ticketed questions.
1282b.type_reasoning: No one is waiting; each question produces a written answer the user relies on.
1282b.unit_reasoning: Written questions arrive as tickets or emails in a queue and are closed one at a time.
1282b.notes: Live versus written share depends heavily on whether the desk is phone-first or ticket-first; 1288 covers the investigation behind harder questions and overlaps substantially.

1283a.task_statement: Enter commands and observe system functioning to verify correct operations and detect errors.
1283a.part_text: Run test commands and observe a computer or system after an installation, repair, or change to verify it works correctly.
1283a.work_item: one post-install or post-repair verification of a machine or system
1283a.end: correct operation confirmed and noted on the ticket, or error found and fix reopened
1283a.checked_by: the user; support lead closing the ticket
1283a.split_reasoning: Entering commands and observing systems produces two kinds of item: verifying a machine or system after an install, repair, or change, and routine checks run to catch errors.
1283a.type_reasoning: Each verification ends in a pass/fail judgment that the user or ticket closure relies on.
1283a.unit_reasoning: Verification is done once per install or fix, and its result is what allows the ticket or job to be closed.
1283a.notes: Part b is close to 1285 (overseeing daily performance); the boundary between the two statements is blurry.

1283b.task_statement: Enter commands and observe system functioning to verify correct operations and detect errors.
1283b.part_text: Run routine diagnostic commands on systems to detect errors before users report them.
1283b.work_item: one routine system check round (e.g. daily check of servers, printers, network links)
1283b.end: results recorded, with any errors logged as tickets
1283b.checked_by: IT supervisor; systems administrators who act on the errors
1283b.split_reasoning: Entering commands and observing systems produces two kinds of item: verifying a machine or system after an install, repair, or change, and routine checks run to catch errors.
1283b.type_reasoning: Routine checking is continuing work, but each run produces a recorded result that others rely on.
1283b.unit_reasoning: Routine checks are done as a scheduled round (e.g. a morning check of key systems) and recorded as a whole.
1283b.notes: Part b is close to 1285 (overseeing daily performance); the boundary between the two statements is blurry.

1284b.task_statement: Install and perform minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications.
1284b.part_text: Install software or make minor software repairs (reinstall, patch, reconfigure) on a user's computer following installation specifications.
1284b.work_item: one software installation or minor software repair completed on a machine
1284b.end: software installed or fixed and ticket closed
1284b.split_reasoning: Two different kinds of work: hands-on installation and repair of hardware and peripherals, and installing or fixing software at a computer.
1284b.type_reasoning: Each install or fix is a separate job done at a computer that the user relies on.
1284b.unit_reasoning: Software installs and fixes come in as individual requests or tickets and are closed one at a time.
1284b.notes: Hardware/software split share is a judgment; remote software deployment makes part b more common in some sites.

1285a.task_statement: Oversee the daily performance of computer systems.
1285a.part_text: Follow up a performance problem or alert on a computer system during the day and decide what action is needed.
1285a.work_item: one performance alert or problem followed up
1285a.start: alert raised or slowdown noticed or reported
1285a.end: cause recorded and fix applied, escalated, or closed as no action
1285a.split_reasoning: Overseeing daily performance is continuous; it produces two kinds of item: problems or alerts followed up, and a daily status check of the systems.
1285a.type_reasoning: Each problem followed up ends in a decision and a ticket note others rely on.
1285a.unit_reasoning: Alerts and performance problems are the unit that enters the queue and gets closed.
1285a.notes: 'Oversee' is vague; for a user support specialist this is likely a modest share of time, and it overlaps heavily with 1283.

1286b.task_statement: Set up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software.
1286b.part_text: Install and configure the operating system, software, and accounts on a new employee's computer so it is ready for use.
1286b.work_item: one workstation configured and handed over to an employee
1286b.start: setup request or new-starter ticket received with hardware available
1286b.end: machine imaged, software and accounts configured, handed to employee and ticket closed
1286b.split_reasoning: Setting up equipment is partly hands-on (unpacking, placing, cabling) and partly at a computer (installing and configuring the operating system and software), so it is split.
1286b.type_reasoning: Each configured machine is a distinct deliverable handed to the employee.
1286b.unit_reasoning: Machines are set up one per new starter or replacement request, and handed over as a whole.
1286b.notes: 'Ensuring proper installation' may mean checking others' work; treated as part of the same setup items.

1287a.task_statement: Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.
1287a.part_text: Write up the record of a user problem and the remedial action taken in the ticketing system after it is handled.
1287a.work_item: one problem-and-remedy record written up for a ticket
1287a.end: ticket notes complete with problem, steps taken, and outcome; ticket closed or updated
1287a.checked_by: help-desk lead; other support staff who pick up the ticket later
1287a.split_reasoning: The statement covers two kinds of record: a record of each problem and the remedy taken, and running logs of daily data communication transactions and installation activities.
1287a.type_reasoning: Each record is a written item colleagues and supervisors rely on.
1287a.unit_reasoning: One record per problem or ticket is the unit others read and audit.
1287a.notes: Some ticket notes are typed while the user is still on the line; treated here as wrap-up work done after the contact, which may understate a live share.

1287b.task_statement: Maintain records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities.
1287b.part_text: Keep the daily log of data communication transactions and installation activities.
1287b.work_item: one day's log of transactions and installation activities
1287b.end: day's entries complete and log filed
1287b.split_reasoning: The statement covers two kinds of record: a record of each problem and the remedy taken, and running logs of daily data communication transactions and installation activities.
1287b.type_reasoning: Logs are continuing, but each day's log is a record others rely on.
1287b.unit_reasoning: The log is maintained and reviewed per day or shift.
1287b.notes: Some ticket notes are typed while the user is still on the line; treated here as wrap-up work done after the contact, which may understate a live share.

1288b.task_statement: Read technical manuals, confer with users, or conduct computer diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems or to provide technical assistance and support.
1288b.part_text: Investigate and resolve a ticketed computer problem after the contact, using diagnostics, technical manuals, and follow-up with the user.
1288b.work_item: one ticketed problem investigated and resolved
1288b.start: ticket assigned or problem left open from a contact
1288b.end: fix applied and confirmed by the user, ticket closed, or ticket escalated
1288b.split_reasoning: Reading manuals, conferring with users, and running diagnostics are alternative means to one deliverable (a resolved problem), but the work is done in two places: live while the user waits, and afterwards on ticketed problems.
1288b.type_reasoning: No one is waiting; each investigation produces a resolution that the user relies on.
1288b.unit_reasoning: Harder problems become tickets that are worked and closed one at a time.
1288b.notes: Strong overlap with 1282; the two statements describe largely the same problem-resolution workflow from different angles.

1290a.task_statement: Develop training materials and procedures, or train users in the proper use of hardware or software.
1290a.part_text: Write training materials or procedures for the proper use of hardware or software.
1290a.work_item: one training guide, how-to document, or procedure
1290a.start: need for material identified (new system, recurring question)
1290a.end: material reviewed and published to users or the knowledge base
1290a.checked_by: IT supervisor; users who follow it
1290a.split_reasoning: Two different activities joined by 'or': writing training materials and procedures, and training users.
1290a.type_reasoning: Produces a document or guide that users and colleagues rely on.
1290a.unit_reasoning: Materials are written and released one guide, procedure, or course pack at a time.
1290a.notes: Share between writing and delivering training is a judgment and varies by organization.

1291a.task_statement: Refer major hardware or software problems or defective products to vendors or technicians for service.
1291a.part_text: Refer a major hardware or software problem or a defective product to a vendor or specialist technician for service.
1291a.work_item: one vendor or technician service referral (case or RMA opened)
1291a.start: problem judged beyond in-house repair or product found defective
1291a.end: case opened with vendor with problem details and warranty info, user informed, ticket updated
1291a.checked_by: vendor or technician; the affected user; IT supervisor
1291a.split_reasoning: One activity: referring a major problem or defective product to an outside vendor or technician.
1291a.type_reasoning: Each referral is a distinct service case that the vendor and the user rely on.
1291a.unit_reasoning: Referrals are made as individual vendor service cases or RMAs, each opened and tracked to return.
1291a.notes: Unclear whether follow-up until the item is returned is part of the referral; treated as ending when the case is handed over.

1292a.task_statement: Prepare evaluations of software or hardware, and recommend improvements or upgrades.
1292a.part_text: Evaluate a piece of software or hardware and recommend improvements or upgrades.
1292a.work_item: one evaluation with recommendation (product, upgrade, or improvement)
1292a.start: request or identified need to assess a product or system
1292a.end: evaluation and recommendation sent to IT manager
1292a.split_reasoning: One activity: evaluating software or hardware and writing recommendations; the recommendation is part of the evaluation deliverable.
1292a.type_reasoning: Produces a written evaluation with recommendations that managers read and act on.
1292a.unit_reasoning: The evaluation and its recommendation are handed over together as one document.

1296a.task_statement: Modify and customize commercial programs for internal needs.
1296a.part_text: Modify or customize a commercial program (e.g. templates, macros, configuration, scripts) to meet internal needs.
1296a.work_item: one program customization delivered (template, macro, configuration change)
1296a.end: change tested and released to users
1296a.split_reasoning: One activity: modifying or customizing commercial software for internal needs.
1296a.type_reasoning: Each customization is a distinct change that users rely on.
1296a.unit_reasoning: Customizations are requested and delivered one change at a time.

1297a.task_statement: Conduct office automation feasibility studies, including workflow analysis, space design, or cost comparison analysis.
1297a.part_text: Conduct an office automation feasibility study, including workflow analysis, space design, or cost comparison.
1297a.work_item: one office automation feasibility study report
1297a.end: study with analysis and recommendation delivered to management
1297a.checked_by: IT manager; office or department management
1297a.split_reasoning: Workflow analysis, space design, and cost comparison are components of one deliverable, the feasibility study.
1297a.type_reasoning: Produces a study report that management reads and decides on.
1297a.unit_reasoning: The study is handed over and signed off as one report.
1297a.notes: Studies may be large; a single report could be close to project scale. Some site visits for space design may be physical, but they are minor.

15204a.task_statement: Hire, supervise, and direct workers engaged in special project work, problem-solving, monitoring, and installation of data communication equipment and software.
15204a.part_text: Hire workers for special project, monitoring, and installation work: screen candidates, interview, and decide on hires.
15204a.end: candidate selected and recommendation or offer sent to HR
15204a.split_reasoning: Two different activities: hiring workers, and supervising and directing them day to day.
15204a.type_reasoning: Each hiring process ends in a hiring decision that HR and management rely on.
15204a.unit_reasoning: Hiring is handled one vacancy at a time and signed off as a decision.
15204a.notes: Interviewing is itself interpersonal; part a is coded at the level of the hiring decision.

2578a.task_statement: Keep records of customer interactions or transactions, recording details of inquiries, complaints, or comments, as well as actions taken.
2578a.part_text: Enter details of the customer's inquiry, complaint, or comment and the actions taken into the account notes while the customer is on the line or at the desk.

2578a.end: notes and actions logged on the account before the contact ends

2578a.unit_reasoning: Notes are attached to one contact and are written within that contact.

2578b.task_statement: Keep records of customer interactions or transactions, recording details of inquiries, complaints, or comments, as well as actions taken.
2578b.part_text: Complete the interaction or transaction record (disposition codes, summary, actions taken) in after-call wrap-up.
2578b.work_item: one interaction record completed after a call or visit
2578b.end: record saved with disposition code, summary, and actions taken

2578b.split_reasoning: One activity, recording each contact, but done in two places: notes typed while the customer is still on the line, and the wrap-up record completed after the contact ends.
2578b.type_reasoning: Done after the contact ends with no one waiting, producing a record others rely on.
2578b.unit_reasoning: Each contact gets one closed record in the CRM, which is what QA samples and later agents read.
2578b.notes: The live versus wrap-up share depends on the center's after-call-work policy.

2579a.task_statement: Resolve customers' service or billing complaints by performing activities such as exchanging merchandise, refunding money, or adjusting bills.
2579a.part_text: Process an exchange, refund, or bill adjustment while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
2579a.work_item: one refund, exchange, or bill adjustment entered during a call or visit
2579a.start: customer agrees to the proposed remedy
2579a.end: refund, exchange, or adjustment entered and confirmed to the customer
2579a.checked_by: the customer, and supervisor or finance for adjustments above limits
2579a.split_reasoning: One activity, carrying out a remedy for a complaint, but done in two places: during the call or visit while the customer waits, and afterwards from queued or written cases.
2579a.type_reasoning: The remedy is entered and confirmed during the live contact while the customer waits.
2579a.unit_reasoning: Each remedy is agreed and entered within one contact.
2579a.notes: Where reps also staff a physical returns desk, merchandise handling would add a PHYSICAL component; treated as atypical for this occupation.

2579b.task_statement: Resolve customers' service or billing complaints by performing activities such as exchanging merchandise, refunding money, or adjusting bills.
2579b.part_text: Process the refund, exchange, or bill adjustment for a written or escalated complaint after the contact, once the remedy has been decided.
2579b.work_item: one refund, exchange, or bill adjustment processed from a queued case
2579b.start: case with an approved or decided remedy reaches the representative's queue
2579b.end: refund, exchange, or adjustment entered or submitted and the case noted
2579b.checked_by: supervisor and billing or finance team
2579b.split_reasoning: One activity, carrying out a remedy for a complaint, but done in two places: during the call or visit while the customer waits, and afterwards from queued or written cases.
2579b.type_reasoning: Done from a queue of cases with no customer waiting, ending in a processed remedy transaction.
2579b.unit_reasoning: Each remedy transaction is entered or submitted as one item that billing or finance relies on; investigating the complaint and notifying the customer are covered by 2585 and 2581.
2579b.notes: Where reps also staff a physical returns desk, merchandise handling would add a PHYSICAL component; treated as atypical for this occupation.

2580a.task_statement: Check to ensure that appropriate changes were made to resolve customers' problems.
2580a.part_text: Check the account or order system to confirm that the change made to resolve a customer's problem was carried out correctly.
2580a.work_item: one resolution verified for a customer case
2580a.start: follow-up date reached or confirmation of change expected
2580a.end: change confirmed and case closed, or discrepancy flagged and case reopened
2580a.split_reasoning: One activity: following up to confirm that a remedy actually took effect.
2580a.type_reasoning: Done after the contact as a follow-up, producing a verified (or reopened) case.
2580a.unit_reasoning: Follow-up checks are tied to one case and close or reopen it.
2580a.notes: Some checks happen immediately during the original call; this coding assumes the typical follow-up after the contact.

2581a.task_statement: Contact customers to respond to inquiries or to notify them of claim investigation results or any planned adjustments.
2581a.part_text: Write and send a response to a customer's inquiry or a notification of claim investigation results or a planned adjustment.
2581a.work_item: one written response or notification sent to a customer
2581a.start: inquiry or investigation result ready for response
2581a.end: letter or email sent and logged on the account
2581a.checked_by: the customer, and supervisor or QA reviewer
2581a.split_reasoning: One activity, contacting customers with answers or results, but done by two channels with different workflows: written responses and outbound phone calls.
2581a.type_reasoning: Produces a letter or email the customer relies on, with no one waiting.
2581a.unit_reasoning: Each response or notification is sent individually and closes an item in the queue.
2581a.notes: Outbound calls are initiated by the representative, which fits LIVE_SERVICE only loosely; channel mix varies by employer.

2581b.task_statement: Contact customers to respond to inquiries or to notify them of claim investigation results or any planned adjustments.
2581b.part_text: Call a customer back to answer an inquiry or explain claim investigation results or a planned adjustment.
2581b.work_item: one outbound callback delivering an answer or result
2581b.end: result explained, customer's questions answered, call ended
2581b.checked_by: the customer, and QA reviewer of recorded calls
2581b.split_reasoning: One activity, contacting customers with answers or results, but done by two channels with different workflows: written responses and outbound phone calls.
2581b.type_reasoning: The explanation happens in a live conversation with the customer on the line.
2581b.unit_reasoning: Each callback is one contact that delivers the result and answers follow-up questions.
2581b.notes: Outbound calls are initiated by the representative, which fits LIVE_SERVICE only loosely; channel mix varies by employer.

2582a.task_statement: Refer unresolved customer grievances to designated departments for further investigation.
2582a.part_text: Prepare and route a referral of an unresolved customer grievance to the designated department for investigation.
2582a.start: representative determines the grievance cannot be resolved at first level
2582a.end: referral with case details submitted to the designated department
2582a.split_reasoning: One activity: escalating an unresolved grievance to another department.
2582a.type_reasoning: Produces an escalation ticket that the receiving department relies on, usually completed after the contact.
2582a.unit_reasoning: Escalations are handed over as tickets or referral forms, one per grievance.
2582a.notes: The customer is often told of the escalation during the call, but writing the referral is usually wrap-up work.

2583a.task_statement: Determine charges for services requested, collect deposits or payments, or arrange for billing.
2583a.part_text: Determine the charges for a requested service and collect a deposit or payment, or set up billing, while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
2583a.work_item: one service charge determined and payment or billing arrangement completed during a contact
2583a.end: charge quoted, payment or deposit taken or billing arranged, receipt or confirmation given
2583a.checked_by: the customer, and cash-office or billing reconciliation
2583a.split_reasoning: One activity: pricing a requested service and taking payment or setting up billing; quoting, collecting, and arranging billing are alternative ways to settle the same transaction.
2583a.type_reasoning: Charges are quoted and payment taken while the customer waits.
2583a.unit_reasoning: Each charge-and-payment transaction is completed within one contact.
2583a.notes: Some billing arrangements may be completed later in the back office; assumed small.

2584a.task_statement: Complete contract forms, prepare change of address records, or issue service discontinuance orders, using computers.
2584a.part_text: Complete a contract form, change-of-address record, or service discontinuance order in the computer while the customer is on the line or at the desk.
2584a.work_item: one account order (contract, address change, or discontinuance) entered during a contact
2584a.end: order submitted and confirmation given to the customer
2584a.checked_by: the customer and the fulfilment or billing team that acts on the order
2584a.split_reasoning: One activity, entering account paperwork, but done in two places: during the call or visit and afterwards from mailed or emailed requests.
2584a.type_reasoning: The order is entered while the customer waits and is confirmed to them.
2584a.unit_reasoning: Each order is entered and confirmed within one contact.
2584a.notes: 18565 includes 'enter orders' and 'cancel accounts', which overlaps part a.

2584b.task_statement: Complete contract forms, prepare change of address records, or issue service discontinuance orders, using computers.
2584b.part_text: Process contract forms, change-of-address records, or discontinuance orders from written or online requests.
2584b.work_item: one account order processed from a written request
2584b.end: order entered and confirmation sent to the customer
2584b.checked_by: the customer and the fulfilment or billing team
2584b.split_reasoning: One activity, entering account paperwork, but done in two places: during the call or visit and afterwards from mailed or emailed requests.
2584b.type_reasoning: Done from a back-office queue with no one waiting.
2584b.unit_reasoning: Written requests are worked as individual items in a queue.
2584b.notes: 18565 includes 'enter orders' and 'cancel accounts', which overlaps part a.

2585a.task_statement: Obtain and examine all relevant information to assess validity of complaints and to determine possible causes, such as extreme weather conditions that could increase utility bills.
2585a.part_text: Look up account and usage information during the call to assess whether a complaint is valid and explain the likely cause.

2585a.end: validity and likely cause explained to the customer and noted
2585a.split_reasoning: Different kinds of item: quick validity checks done during the call, and longer investigations of complaints done afterwards.
2585a.type_reasoning: The lookup and assessment happen while the customer is on the line.
2585a.unit_reasoning: Each assessment is completed and explained within one contact.
2585a.notes: The split between quick and deep assessments varies a lot by industry.

2585b.task_statement: Obtain and examine all relevant information to assess validity of complaints and to determine possible causes, such as extreme weather conditions that could increase utility bills.
2585b.part_text: Gather and examine records and outside information to investigate a complaint's validity and cause after the contact.
2585b.work_item: one complaint investigation with a validity finding
2585b.end: finding on validity and cause recorded and passed for remedy or reply
2585b.checked_by: supervisor, and the staff who decide the remedy
2585b.split_reasoning: Different kinds of item: quick validity checks done during the call, and longer investigations of complaints done afterwards.
2585b.type_reasoning: Produces a written finding on the case that decides the remedy, with no one waiting.
2585b.unit_reasoning: Investigations are worked as cases and closed with a finding.
2585b.notes: The split between quick and deep assessments varies a lot by industry.

2587a.task_statement: Review insurance policy terms to determine whether a particular loss is covered by insurance.
2587a.part_text: Read the policy terms and tell a caller whether their loss appears to be covered while they are on the line.

2587a.start: customer describes the loss and asks whether it is covered
2587a.end: coverage answer given and noted on the account

2587a.split_reasoning: One activity, deciding whether a loss is covered, but done in two places: answering a caller's coverage question live, and reviewing coverage on a claim afterwards.
2587a.type_reasoning: The policy is reviewed and the answer given while the customer waits.
2587a.unit_reasoning: Each coverage question is answered within one contact.
2587a.notes: Applies only to insurance-sector representatives; the live share is a guess.

2587b.task_statement: Review insurance policy terms to determine whether a particular loss is covered by insurance.
2587b.part_text: Review the policy terms against a reported loss and record a coverage determination for the claim.
2587b.work_item: one coverage determination for a reported loss
2587b.end: coverage decision recorded on the claim file
2587b.checked_by: claims adjuster or supervisor, and the customer
2587b.split_reasoning: One activity, deciding whether a loss is covered, but done in two places: answering a caller's coverage question live, and reviewing coverage on a claim afterwards.
2587b.type_reasoning: Produces a coverage determination on a claim file, with no one waiting.
2587b.unit_reasoning: Coverage is determined per claim and recorded on the file.
2587b.notes: Applies only to insurance-sector representatives; the live share is a guess.

2589b.task_statement: Compare disputed merchandise with original requisitions and information from invoices and prepare invoices for returned goods.
2589b.part_text: Match the dispute against requisition and invoice records and prepare an invoice for the returned goods.
2589b.work_item: one return invoice prepared for a disputed shipment
2589b.start: disputed goods and original requisition and invoice in hand
2589b.end: return invoice issued and sent to billing and the customer
2589b.checked_by: billing or accounts receivable, and the customer
2589b.split_reasoning: Two activities: hands-on comparison of the returned merchandise, and desk work matching documents and preparing the return invoice.
2589b.type_reasoning: Produces a return invoice that billing and the customer rely on.

2591a.task_statement: Recommend improvements in products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing methods and procedures to prevent future problems.
2591a.part_text: Write a recommendation to management for an improvement in products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing procedures based on recurring customer problems.
2591a.start: recurring problem identified from customer contacts
2591a.end: recommendation with supporting examples sent to supervisor or process owner
2591a.checked_by: supervisor or the department that owns the process
2591a.split_reasoning: One activity: proposing changes to prevent recurring problems.
2591a.type_reasoning: Produces a written suggestion that managers read and act on.
2591a.unit_reasoning: Recommendations are submitted individually through a suggestion form, email, or team meeting note.

18565a.task_statement: Confer with customers by telephone or in person to provide information about products or services, take or enter orders, cancel accounts, or obtain details of complaints.
18565a.part_text: Answer a customer's call or visit asking for information about products or services.
18565a.work_item: one information inquiry answered during a call or visit
18565a.end: customer confirms the question is answered, contact ends
18565a.split_reasoning: All live contacts, but covering different kinds of item: information requests, orders and cancellations entered on the spot, and complaint intake.
18565a.type_reasoning: The answer is given in a live conversation while the customer waits.
